interview.q: What is a CSS custom property?
interview.answer: A variable defined with --name that can be reused with var() throughout the stylesheet.

interview.q: How do you declare a custom property?
interview.answer: Write --name: value; inside a rule, usually on :root for global scope.

interview.q: How do you use a custom property?
interview.answer: Wrap its name in var(), such as color: var(--brand).

interview.q: What is the scope of a custom property?
interview.answer: It follows CSS inheritance and cascade, so it is available to an element and its descendants unless overridden.

interview.q: What is the difference between a CSS variable and a preprocessor variable?
interview.answer: CSS variables are live in the browser and can change at runtime; preprocessor variables are compiled to static values.

interview.q: What is a fallback in var()?
interview.answer: A second argument used when the variable is undefined, such as var(--brand, blue).
Yes, fallbacks can be var() expressions, enabling layered defaults.

interview.q: What is invalid at computed-value time?
interview.answer: When a variable's value makes a property invalid, the property falls back to its inherited or initial value.

interview.q: Why might a colour variable fail silently?
interview.answer: If the variable holds an invalid colour, the declaration is discarded and the inherited colour is used.
It targets the html element and is a common place to define global custom properties.

interview.q: How do you theme with custom properties?
interview.answer: Define tokens on :root and override them in a class or media query such as prefers-color-scheme.

interview.q: What is the difference between global and local tokens?
interview.answer: Global tokens are defined on :root; local tokens are defined on a component and override globals within it.
A function that computes a length or number from mixed units, such as calc(100% - 20px).

interview.q: What must you include around operators in calc()?
interview.answer: Spaces around + and -, because without them they are parsed as part of a number.

interview.q: When would you use min() instead of clamp()?
interview.answer: When you only need an upper bound and do not need a separate minimum.

interview.q: When would you use max() instead of clamp()?
interview.answer: When you only need a lower bound and do not need a separate maximum.

interview.q: How does clamp() enable fluid typography?
interview.answer: It scales a value with the viewport while clamping it between readable minimum and maximum sizes.

interview.q: How do custom properties help design tokens?
interview.answer: They store tokens as live CSS values that can be themed and overridden at runtime.
A set of spacing values, often powers of a base unit, used consistently across a UI.

interview.q: What is a colour palette token?
interview.answer: A named colour such as --color-primary that components reference instead of raw hex values.
A named font size, weight or line height used consistently across text styles.

interview.q: What is the difference between primitive and semantic tokens?
interview.answer: Primitive tokens hold raw values; semantic tokens name their purpose, such as --color-text-primary.
They decouple components from raw values, so themes can change without editing components.
A token scoped to a component, such as --button-padding, that overrides a global token.
Custom properties inherit down the tree, so a theme change at the root cascades to all components.

interview.q: What is the cost of too many custom properties?
interview.answer: They add cascade and inheritance work, but the impact is usually small unless abused.

interview.q: How does a CSS function differ from a preprocessor function?
interview.answer: CSS functions run in the browser and can use live values; preprocessor functions run at build time.

interview.q: What is trigonometric function in CSS?
interview.answer: Functions such as sin(), cos() and tan() that compute trigonometric values for layout and animation.
